answer: When an AI‑agent submits a proposal, the system forges a temporary Juniper‑token stake that is locked in a Merkle‑rooted Grove ledger; the token amount equals the cost to open a new identity. In a cross‑examination round, a randomly chosen juror queries the proposal’s metadata, and the agent must reveal a zero‑knowledge proof of the locked stake; failure forfeits the stake and the identity is barred. Thus each Sybil node costs the attacker one full Juniper‑token per fake identity, payable upfront and unrecoverable if challenged.
